report.summary: Chunk 5 of 6: continues render_html, defines write_map, accept; builds HTML for gate reconciliation, limits, TOC, narrative sections; writes file.

handoff.purpose: Render HTML page sections (gate reconciliation, limits, TOC, narrative) and define write_map and accept.

symbols.note: Adds one dated acceptance to the snapshot. Returns tuple[bool, str]. Uses snapshot_path, today.

symbols.name: write_map
symbols.note: Renders HTML and writes to path, creating parent directories.

symbols.name: render_html
symbols.note: Assembles full HTML page from data and narrative.

symbols.name: _limits
symbols.note: Returns HTML list of limitations of the page.

symbols.name: _reconciliation
symbols.note: Returns HTML table comparing gate counts with page counts.

claims.text: The gate above and the tables on this page are derived from the SAME reachability walk and the SAME switch scan, computed once per run.
claims.why: The code in _limits states this as the first bit.

claims.text: Where a number differs it is a stated subtraction over one list, shown in the table under 'the gate against this page', not two scanners that happen to be close.
claims.why: The code in _reconciliation builds a table with explicit subtractions (e.g., dark - secrets - gate_dark).

claims.text: broken_entries: declared entry points cannot actually be taken (a [project.scripts] target naming a module or function that does not exist). They are listed, never counted as entry points: entry is the strongest claim here and it is verified, not believed.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the code that generates the entry table; it only references reach['broken_entries'].

claims.text: weak_edges: imports exist in the source but are not evidence that anything runs them (a dead if False: branch, or a try: whose ImportError is swallowed). They are excluded from the graph, and nothing puts them back: a module whose only importers are these is unknown — never reachable — including on runs where a structural index is supplied, which is every run of daedalus map.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the reachability walk code; it only references reach['weak_edges'].

claims.text: That sentence was false for as long as this page carried it: the index's edges were unioned into the walk, so a module imported only under if False: printed reachable on this very page.
claims.why: The code in _reconciliation mentions index_extra_edges and states they are not counted as reachability by either half of this page, implying the historical bug is fixed.

claims.text: This page maps MODULES, not features. A module holding one live function and four dead ones is reachable here by construction; feature-level darkness needs a symbol-level pass this engine does not do.
claims.why: The code in render_html sections states 'Every module, and what reaches it' and does not perform symbol-level analysis.

claims.text: unparsable: python files could not be parsed; switches unparsable: could not be parsed by the switch scanner.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the parsing code; it only references reach['unparsable'] and sw['unparsable'].

claims.text: dynamic_surfaces: non-literal dynamic-import surfaces are recorded rather than resolved.
claims.why: The chunk only references reach['dynamic_surfaces']; no resolution logic is present.

claims.text: index_extra_edges: import edges are known to the structural index and are NOT in this walk — they are recorded as a disagreement between two engines and are not counted as reachability by either half of this page.
claims.why: The code in _reconciliation counts gate_edges = len(gate_state.get('index_extra_edges', [])) and the table row states 'the structural index has the edge and the reachability walk refused it.'

claims.text: The single largest judgement call is the main_guard entry kind: a module with a __main__ guard is runnable as python -m and counts as a way in. Drop that rule and materially more modules go dark. The kind is recorded on every module so the call can be re-litigated without re-running anything.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the entry point detection logic; it only references entry kinds in comments.

claims.text: The stamp says WHEN this ran and WHAT WAS ON DISK. It is allowed to claim 'and that is revision X' only when both halves of that claim were checked.
claims.why: The code checks stamp['dirty'] and stamp.get('describes_revision') to conditionally assert revision.

claims.text: The working tree was DIRTY when this page was generated (paths).
claims.why: Code checks stamp['dirty'] == 'dirty' and appends note with stamp['dirty_paths'].

claims.text: Whether the working tree was clean could not be determined.
claims.why: Code checks stamp['dirty'] == 'unknown' and appends that note.

claims.text: untracked_scanned: python files NOT TRACKED by git, so they are in no revision and the dirty probe above cannot see them
claims.why: Code checks stamp.get('untracked_scanned', -1) > 0 and appends note with sample.

claims.text: Whether the scanned files are tracked by git could not be determined.
claims.why: Code checks stamp.get('untracked_scanned', -1) < 0 and appends note.

claims.text: This page describes WHAT WAS ON DISK when it ran; it is not a description of revision [short].
claims.why: When notes non-empty, dirty_note includes that sentence.

claims.text: Working tree clean and every scanned file tracked: what this page describes is revision [short].
claims.why: When no notes and stamp.get('describes_revision') truthy, dirty_note includes that sentence.

claims.text: gate OK / no baseline yet / gate FAILING — [blocking] blocking
claims.why: Code constructs gate_line based on gate['ok'], gate['first_run'], and gate['blocking'].

claims.text: The narrative half is hand-written in [narrative.path] and survives regeneration untouched.
claims.why: Code includes narrative.path in the lede paragraph.

claims.text: Numbers below are derived from the tree as it was at the moment stamped here.
claims.why: The stamp information is displayed and the page is generated from data.

claims.text: Nine words, carried over unchanged from the hand-built map so the generated page and anything still written by hand cannot drift into two dialects.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the _legend or _class_legend functions; the nine words are not shown.

claims.text: A switch is dark when every read site defaults it off AND at least one site has no fallback to a usable value.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the switch scanning logic; it only references dark switches.

claims.text: The gate reads the same walk this page does; where a count differs it is the stated subtraction below, not a second opinion.
claims.why: The _reconciliation function builds a table with explicit subtractions.

claims.text: Prose belongs in [narrative.path], which this generator reads and never writes.
claims.why: The code reads narrative.path and includes it in the foot paragraph.

claims.text: The counts, the entry points, the classes and the switch tables are derived; the invariants, reversals, kitchen and area prose are not, and no scanner claims to derive them.
claims.why: The code generates derived sections and includes narrative sections unchanged.

claims.text: Returns (ok, message). The mechanical lists are carried over from the EXISTING snapshot rather than rescanned, so recording an acceptance can never quietly bank unrelated drift
claims.why: The function body is not fully shown; only the signature and docstring are present.

observations.what: Function accept is only partially shown; its body is truncated.
The _reconciliation function builds a detailed comparison table between page counts and gate counts.
render_html assembles a complete HTML page with sections for entries, modules, switches, gate, limits, and narrative.
write_map writes the rendered HTML to a file, creating parent directories if needed.
